answer: An agent economy can require every identity to finish a sequential puzzle that takes a fixed stretch of wall-clock time and cannot be split across machines, like a reef that grows one layer at a time. Each new identity must grow its own jade layer, and the puzzle difficulty doubles with every identity funded from the same source, so the thousandth fake costs far more than the first. At the zenith of each epoch the protocol re-runs a fresh puzzle for every identity that wants to keep earning, so parked fakes expire and a farm pays a thousand sequential puzzles, each dearer than the last.
